issues.span: Blessed One, it is wonderful to what supreme extent
issues.evidence: The Tibetan has the ཇི་སྙེད་པས ... ནི topic clauses followed by a single exclamation བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ངོ་མཚར་ལགས་སོ, then བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་ངོ་མཚར་ལགས་སོ. The English gives "Blessed One, it is wonderful" twice (once opening the sentence, once after it), i.e. one more exclamation than the Tibetan has.
issues.fix: To what supreme extent the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and to what supreme extent the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings — Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!

issues.span: however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings
issues.evidence: Tibetan: སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་གདགས་པའི་བརྟགས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད — "however much the realm of sentient beings is designated as sentient beings". The realm is the thing designated (Sanskrit yāvān kaścit sattvadhātuḥ prajñapyamānaḥ prajñapyate; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-7: སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཅི་ཙམ་དུ་སེམས་ཅན་ཞེས་མིང་གིས་གདགས་པས་བཏགས་པ). The English turns "realm of sentient beings" into a locative container of the beings.
issues.fix: however much of the realm of sentient beings is designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings, all of those

issues.span: as having marks and as being without signs
issues.evidence: Tibetan: མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ; Sanskrit lakṣaṇālakṣaṇatas. The English adds "having" and commits to a split reading (marks present, signs absent). Commentaries differ: Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-23 reads བདེན་པར་གྲུབ་པའི་མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར — without truly established marks and signs; Kamalaśīla 3-51 reads མཚན་གྱིས་བལྟ ... མཚན་མེད་པ་ནི་དོན་དམ་པར; Vasubandhu 2-20 reads མཚན་དང་མཚན་མེད་པར. The Tibetan itself does not say "having".
issues.fix: Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as mark and as without sign.

issues.evidence: The Tibetan of this segment ends ... ཉོན་མོངས་པ་མེད་པར་གནས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མཆོག་ཡིན་ཏེ། with no verb of declaring; the verb ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ལགས་སོ occurs only in the next segment (7-31), where the English renders it again. The English thus places the negated verb here as well, duplicating it across the two segments.
issues.fix: the Tathāgata, concerning me, [would say]: "The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction," —
